q: briatico the deepest line in this archive, and the one that does not carry the surname. a small comune on the tyrrhenian coast of briatico — the mazza archive vibo valentia, calabria briatico the deepest line in this archive, and the one that does not carry the surname. a small comune on the tyrrhenian coast of calabria that sent its people to three different continents. 106 people recorded at briatico or its hamlets 1697 the earliest birth the archive can name here 8 generations of prostamo, unbroken the town briatico stands on the tyrrhenian coast about ten kilometres north of vibo valentia, on the stretch italians call the costa degli dei . the town the family left is not quite the town on the map today: old briatico was wrecked by the calabrian earthquake of 1783 and again in 1905 , and the modern comune is a rebuilding, a little inland of the ruins. its hamlets — potenzoni , mandaradoni , san costantino — appear in this archive as birthplaces in their own right, which is how calabrian registers recorded them. that 1783 earthquake matters for a practical reason. it destroyed archives across the province, and it is one of the reasons a line that reaches 1697 here is unusual enough to be worth checking rather than assuming. the families 34 surnames are recorded at briatico in this archive. five of them are ancestral to the brisbane family. anile · averta · barbuto q: method an archive is only worth reading if it says which of its claims are documents, which are inferences, and which are thing method — the mazza archive how this archive decides what it knows method an archive is only worth reading if it says which of its claims are documents, which are inferences, and which are things the family remembers. these are the rules, and they are the same rules as the falco archive. the five words all seven of these family archives grade a claim with the same five words, so a level means the same thing wherever you meet it. the word is always printed next to the colour, because a reader should never have to know the palette to know the confidence. documented a record was read, and it says this. the source is named. probable the evidence points one way and nothing found so far points the other. not proven. inferred reasoned from what is known — a gap of the right size, a name in the right place — rather than witnessed in a record. family told, remembered, or written on a family chart. kept, because discarding it would lose the lead; labelled, because it is not evidence. disputed two sources disagree and neither has been ruled out. both are shown. not claimed some pages carry this instead. it states the thing a reader is likely to assume — the connection that would be tidy, the identification that almost works — and says plainly that this archive does not assert it. an archive is judged as much by what it refuses to say as by what it says. almost everything in this archive currently sits at the family level of the ladder above: asserted by the family tree , and not yet by a document. the tree this site was built from is a myheritage tree contributed by michael mazza and relatives. where it cites ancestry indexes, this site says so; where it cites nothing — which is most of it — this site says that too. converting those assertions into documents is the work. dates, and who does not get one the companion falco archive names living relatives and publishes nothing else about them at all. that rule was tried here first and it failed badly: the test it rests on treats a person as possibly alive unless the tree records a death — and 414 of these 596 people have no death recorded , because most of this tree is undated , not alive . only 68 people in it have a death anywhere. suppressing seven-tenths of an archive makes it unreadable without making anybody safer. so this archive uses a narrower rule, set by david on 10 september 2026: anyone who would be 80 or younger today, and whose death is not recorded, has their dates withheld. their name, their places, their family, their photographs and their records are all published. only the dates are held back. that

burying ground of northern brisbane since the 1860s. it is run by the archdiocese, not the city council, which is why it does not appear in the brisbane city council grave search and why the family tree recorded the cemetery but never a plot. the archdiocese keeps its own register, and it was read on 10 september 2026 . it supplies a plot, a register number, a date of birth, a date of death and piedimonte etneo on etna, briatico on the tyrrhenian coast, and scilla on the strait — about six hundred kilometres apart, in families that had never met. they arrived in australia between 1949 and piedimonte etneo the town on the north-east flank of etna that gave this family its surname — and, of the four quarters, the one the archive knows least about. 40 people placed at piedimonte etneo 1879 the earliest mazza birth with a date 7 mazza here who are joined to nothing the town piedimonte etneo means the foot of the mountain, and it is exactly that: a comune of the province of catania standing on the north-eastern slope of etna , above fiumefreddo and the alcantara valley, looking out at the ionian sea. the neighbouring towns in this archive — mascali , giarre , linguaglossa 's side of the mountain — are all within a few kilometres. living on etna is a recurring administrative fact, not a metaphor. in 1928 the eruption that destroyed the town of mascali — the only town etna has swallowed whole in modern times — happened eight years after sebastiano mazza was born here, and the archive records mascali as a birthplace for people in this family. the line that carries the name, and stops three men, and then nothing. generation 3 rosario mazza — no dates, no places, no record. he exists only because his son's record names him. — generation 2 salvatore mazza — born at piedimonte etneo, died at catania. married maria nicotra . 1879–1929 generation 1 sebastiano mazza — born here, arrived fremantle 4 october 1949, died at brisbane and buried at nudgee . 1920–2002 four generations. it is the shortest of the four quarters by five generations, and the surname the whole archive is named after runs out at a man about whom precisely one fact is known: that he was salvatore's father. the hundred and eleven the family tree also contains 7 mazza of piedimonte etneo — mariano, leonardo, orazio, umberto, giuseppa, serena, graziella and the rest — who form a complete little world of their own: parents, children, marriages, cousins. not one record joins them to sebastiano's line. they are almost certainly the same family. a town of a few thousand people does not produce two unrelated mazza kindreds. but "almost certainly" is not a document, and the join has to be made by a record rather than by an assumption — most likely by the birth act of salvatore mazza, 1879 , which would name his father rosario and his father's age, or by rosario's own marriage act . until then this archive keeps them apart and says why. the open questions → name q: scilla the rock at the northern gate of the strait of messina, and the fishing quarter beneath it. two of the four grandparents scilla — the mazza archive reggio calabria scilla the rock at the northern gate of the strait of messina, and the fishing quarter beneath it. two of the four grandparents were born here, four years apart, and did not marry until brisbane. 70 people recorded at scilla 1821 the earliest birth named here 2 of the four quarters begin here the place scilla is the scylla of the odyssey — the rock opposite the whirlpool of charybdis, at the narrowest point of the strait that separates calabria from sicily. the castello ruffo sits on the headland; below it, on the water, is chianalea , a lane of houses built straight into the sea where the boats are moored at the doors. this was a swordfishing town, and it still is. the geography is the point for this family. from chianalea you can see etna on a clear morning. the scilla families and the piedimonte etneo family were looking at each other across thirty kilometres of water for generations — and met on the other side of the world. scilla was levelled by the 1783 earthquake and the tsunami that followed it, when a wave took a large part of the population off the beach at marina grande. as at briatico , that is why the record here begins where it does. the families arena · benedetto · bova · calarco · d'ascoli · donato · pacino · perina · polistena · pontillo · provvidenza · russo · sanfedele · sofi the registers, opened 10 september 2026 an index that names the parents — and misleads scilla is not in familysearch's full-text corpus — four searches place-matched to it returned nothing, and its calabrian holdings are catanzaro and vibo valentia. but antenati has 57 volumes from the archivio di stato di reggio calabria, births from 1850 ; which had heard of the other two. it is not a pedigree: of the 596 people recorded here, all but a handful never continued the line. only 68 of them have a death recorded anywhere — which is a measure q: the name what the surnames in this archive mean, roughly how common they are, and — the useful part — how much that tells you abo the name — the mazza archive mazza, and the nine names around it the name what the surnames in this archive mean, roughly how common they are, and — the useful part — how much that tells you about whether two people who share one are related. mazza mazza is the italian for a club, a mace or a mallet, from the latin mattea . as a surname it was coined in all the usual ways at once: as a nickname for a strong or a violent man, as a trade name for someone who worked with a mallet or a maul, and — most often — from the medieval personal name mazzo , itself a short form of names like giacomazzo and tommazzo. it is one of the most widespread surnames in italy, found from lombardy to sicily, and it was coined independently many times over . there is no founding mazza family. two mazza households in the same sicilian town are much more likely to be related than two mazza in different provinces — but "much more likely" is a probability, and this archive does not publish probabilities as descents. that is precisely the situation at piedimonte etneo , where 118 mazza sit in two groups that no record joins. the others name here where it belongs what it is prostamo 84 briatico, vibo valentia rare, and concentrated. almost the whole italian distribution sits in a few calabrian comuni around vibo valentia. a rare surname in one small place is the best gift a genealogist gets: two prostamo of briatico almost certainly are related. polistena 45 scilla, reggio calabria a toponymic — from the town of polistena in the province of reggio calabria. it marks a family that moved from there, and was named for having done so. arena 39 scilla, reggio calabria very common across calabria and sicily; from arena , sand — a place-name element. common enough that a shared arena surname is worth nothing on its own. the archive holds four undated giuseppe arena and keeps them apart. nicotra 8 piedimonte etneo, catania strongly eastern sicilian, and heavily concentrated around catania — which is exactly where this archive finds it. melluso 12 briatico southern, both sicilian and calabrian; probably from mele , honey, or a diminutive of a personal name. anile 12 briatico / potenzoni calabrian and uncommon, clustered in the vibo valentia area. donato 20 scilla from the personal name donato — "given". common everywhere in the south. cavallaro 13 scilla / brisbane a trade name: a horseman, a groom, a keeper of horses. bova 13 reggio calabria another toponymic — bova is a greek-speaking comune in the far south of calabria. why this page exists because the single commonest error in family histo

q: the queensland register the registry's historical index is free, it is authoritative, and — the part that matters — it can be searched by a fath the queensland register — the mazza archive read 10 september 2026 the queensland register the registry's historical index is free, it is authoritative, and — the part that matters — it can be searched by a father's or a mother's name. one search returned three of sebastiano mazza's siblings. the queensland registry of births, deaths and marriages publishes a searchable historical index: deaths to 1996, marriages to 1951, births to 1926 . every death and birth entry carries the names of both parents , and the search box will take a parent's name as the query. that turns it from a lookup into a reconstruction tool . searching "salvatore mazza" in the father field returns the deaths of his children — and each of those names their mother, which is how a family asserted by the tree became a family on the record. the finding michele mazza was sebastiano's brother michele mazza landed at brisbane on the palermo on 21 april 1925 , aged about sixteen, and died the following year. the family tree asserted he was kin and produced nothing to show it. the archive has carried the question since the day it was built: was he the reason they chose queensland? the registry's index answers it: michali mazza · death registration 14 november 1926 · 1926/c/3983 · father salvatori mazza · mother maria lecota . lecota is the index's rendering of nicotra — and the same search returns rosario mazza, born 1899 , whose parents are given in full as salvatore mazza and maria concetta nicotra . the same couple, spelled properly. so michele mazza was a son of salvatore mazza and maria nicotra , and therefore sebastiano mazza 's elder brother . he came out first, alone, at sixteen. he was dead within nineteen months. twenty-four years later his family followed him to the port he had landed at. the archive should say what it still cannot: whether anyone was waiting for sebastiano in 1949, and whether the family knew where the boy was buried. the index gives a date and a registration number, not a grave. c in the registration means a country event — he did not die in brisbane. four deaths, and what each one proves date name registration father mother 14 november 1926 michali mazza 1926/c/3983 salvatori mazza maria lecota 19 march 1986 rosario mazza (b. 1899) 1986/2455 salvatore mazza maria concetta nicotra 24 september 1963 maria nicotra mazza 1963/b/61348 john nicotra venera cassaneti 3 august 1968 mary rosa mazza 1968/b/936 sebastiano mazza domenica postamo michali mazza — lecota is the index's garbling of nicotra. makes michele a son of salvatore mazza and maria nicotra, and therefore
